A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Video-XL and retain the same underlying VST compression approach. Text, equations, tables, and figures support comparison. v1 has no appendix; v4 includes readable supplementary Sections A–G.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, needle-in-a-haystack results, compression ablations, and qualitative demonstrations.

after.justification: v4 reports original benchmark, efficiency, compression, training, and data experiments, with additional results throughout the supplement.

M1.justification: The interleaved VST/KV compression mechanism remains, but fixed-size chunks become content-dependent intervals using CLIP similarities and depth scores. v4 also introduces progressive compression-ratio training and composite/VICO data curation, replacing v1's image-only training with randomly sampled ratios of 2, 4, and 8.

E1.justification: Training expands from image-only data to single-image, multi-image, video, and synthetic action-order supervision. Evaluation adds VideoVista, VideoChatGPT Bench, MVBench, GQA, POPE, and SEEDBench. MME and MMBench were already evaluated in v1 and are retained.

E2.justification: v4's main comparisons add VideoLLaMA2, Video-CCAM, and PLLaVA, while dropping Claude3-Opus and InternVL-Chat-V1.5 from their corresponding benchmark comparisons. New controlled compression comparisons include pooling, Q-Former, LLaMA-Adapter, and C-Abstractor. Supplementary image comparisons additionally evaluate VoCo-LLaMA.

E3.justification: v4 adds MLVU-test evaluation, memory and FLOPs measurements, a retrieval grid extending to 2048 frames, matched 16× compression comparisons, and testing at an unseen 32× ratio. Supplement D introduces backbone and training-regime controls. The main LLaVA-Next-Video comparator also changes from 7B to 34B.

E4.justification: v1's compression-ratio ablation expands into studies of dynamic compression during training versus testing, interval size, curriculum learning, data mixtures, VICO scaling, backbone choice, and context length. Qualitative comparisons and appendix cases expand substantially. The advertisement example is retained with an added LLaMA-VID comparison; the earlier surveillance-anomaly example is removed.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or formal significance tests. The added experiments do not introduce uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Under revised methods and training, v4 replaces MLVU-dev M-avg 57.0 with 64.9 and VideoMME without/with-subtitle scores 51.0/54.4 with 55.5/61.0. Numerous benchmark, efficiency, ablation, and image results are added. v1's VideoMME duration and VNBench task breakdowns disappear. These replacements do not establish isolated same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: v4 adds the depth-score definition governing adaptive interval boundaries and a detailed computational-cost derivation separating attention and other operations for compressed processing (Supplement D, Equations 7–10). The earlier VST attention formalization is also shortened and revised in Supplement C. The new cost analysis substantially extends the mathematical treatment.

C1.justification: The contribution expands from image-trained visual context summarization to dynamic compression, curriculum learning, and composite/VICO training. v4 adds claims of minimal loss at 16× compression and broader leadership among comparable-size models. Its headline long-context demonstration changes from 1024 frames at nearly 100% accuracy to 2048 frames at about 95%.

C2.justification: v4 introduces explanations of complementary image/video supervision, the need to train with dynamic compression, and attention savings versus additional VST computation. Supplement A newly acknowledges substantial training-memory costs and errors beyond 1000 frames. These substantially expand v1's limited discussion of mechanisms and applicability boundaries.

D1.justification: v4 adds learning rates, batch sizes, training hardware, Adam/ZeRO-2-offload/bf16 settings, benchmark-specific frame budgets, and VICO construction details and prompts. These materially expand reproducibility information beyond v1. However, Section 4.1 specifies linear learning-rate decay while Supplement F specifies cosine decay.

R1.justification: A dedicated related-work section and Supplement B substantially expand positioning against LongVA and VoCo-LLaMA. New sparsity references motivate compression, and VideoLLaMB is credited for the segmentation approach. Conversely, v1's explicit attribution to Activation Beacon and its corresponding reference are removed.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, method, experimental narrative, and conclusion are extensively rewritten. Related work becomes a dedicated section, training is integrated into the method discussion, and detailed material is reorganized into supplementary Sections A–G. 'Visual Context Latent Summarization' is reframed as 'VST Compression.'

P2.justification: The document changes from single-column to two-column layout. v4 adds a radar overview, redraws the architecture, combines retrieval heatmaps with resource plots, and adds data-generation diagrams. The original benchmark tables are consolidated and restructured, with numerous new ablation tables, plots, and qualitative displays.

improvement.justification: v4 addresses v1's limited validation of compression and efficiency through matched alternative-compressor comparisons, quantitative resource measurements, and systematic mechanism and training ablations. Expanded implementation details and explicit limitations further strengthen the paper. These gains are substantial, although conflicting learning-rate schedules and Supplement D's disagreement between training-ablation prose and Table 3 limit reproducibility.
